phenomenon.working_label: rare spontaneous punctate photopsia / phosphene-like event
user_reported_features: brief point-like or pixel-like luminous flash
can be noticed outside sky-viewing contexts
no reported migraine or headache association
closed-eye occurrence unknown because events are unpredictable
not_established: external versus retinal versus neural origin

candidate_families.support: Rod photoreceptors exhibit discrete dark-noise events with waveforms similar to real single-photon responses; newer molecular work supports spontaneous rhodopsin activation as the source of discrete noise.
candidate_families.limits: Photoreceptor dark noise is a demonstrated cellular mechanism, but a direct one-to-one mapping from a single rod event to the reported conscious punctate flash is not established.

sources.title: Origin of Discrete and Continuous Dark Noise in Rod Photoreceptors
The mechanism of photon-like dark noise in rod photoreceptors

candidate_families.support: Vitreoretinal traction can physically stimulate retina and create photopsias without external light.
candidate_families.mismatch: Classically described photopsias are often peripheral/temporal, vertical or dramatic and may associate with floaters, so the user's rare isolated pixel-like event is not a textbook match.

candidate_families.support: Ground experiments and Apollo studies demonstrate that ionizing particles, including cosmic-ray muons, can produce visual sensations or flashes in human observers.
candidate_families.limits: Without a synchronized particle detector, an individual spontaneous visual event cannot be assigned to a cosmic-ray cause.

sources.title: Detection of Cosmic Ray µ-Mesons by the Human Eye
Visual Sensations Produced by Cosmic Ray Muons
NASA Apollo light flash experiment record

candidate_families.mismatch: Typical migraine visual aura develops gradually, spreads over time and commonly lasts about 5-60 minutes, which is a poor fit to a rare instantaneous isolated pixel-like event.

sources.title: The typical duration of migraine aura: a systematic review

observational_discriminators: whether it recurs in a fixed visual-field location
whether it can be seen with eyes closed
simultaneous external camera detection if looking at a scene

medical_firewall.rule: This record is a research differential, not a diagnosis.
medical_firewall.urgent_change_pattern: Sudden increase in flashes, many new floaters, shadow/curtain or new visual-field loss warrants prompt ophthalmic assessment for retinal tear/detachment.
